Google AX: The Climbing Millions of AI Agents

AI agents save status, run loops and wait a long time, which the infrastructure made for microservices cannot handle. The video features Google AX, an open source orchestration layer over Kubernetes, with four primitives, snapshot suspension, failure recovery and gVisor isolation.

Published in 24 September 2026 · 10 min 3 s

  • Agentic engineering

The infrastructure wasn't made for agents.

The way we host software today wasn't made for AI agents. 00:00. Treat agents as applications common web can bring down the system or burst the budget 00:21.

For more than a decade, the cloud, with Kubernetes, has been optimized for microservices: predictable, stateless, responding in milliseconds and forgetting 00:43. The agents are the opposite: they run loops, make decisions, write code, keep a lot of state and wait seconds for the model's response 01:05.

That brings three problems. 01:27:

  • Cost: an agent trapped in a loop fires thousands of API calls without anyone seeing 01:27.
  • Security: models that hallucinate generate and run unknown code 01:27.
  • Gargals: the system tries to schedule millions of microevents whenever an agent stops to think 01:47.

What is Google AX

Google AX (Agent Executor) does not replace Kubernetes: it is a layer of orchestration over it, made for actors who keep state and run for a long time 02:08. It summarizes the complexity in four early declaratives in YAML, Kubernetes style 02:29.

The Four Primitive

  • Task: the smallest execution unit, an isolated sandbox with hard limits of CPU and memory, cheap to create, pause and discard 02:50.
  • Workspace: prepares the environment before the agent wakes up, cloning Git repositories and connecting external servers 03:11.
  • Gateway: locks the exit traffic; the agent only talks with pre-approved addresses, in a zero confidence policy 03:53.
  • Model: centralize API keys and template settings in one place 04:14.

Scale and suspension

AX runs on Agent Substrate. As agents spend most of their time waiting, the system packs up idle sessions. 04:34. According to the video, this allows, in theory, billions of sessions in a common cluster 04:54.

The suspension cycle has three steps 05:15:

  • The agent asks the AI something and waits 05:15.
  • AX takes a snapshot of the agent status and suspends it; processing consumption drops to zero 05:15.
  • When the answer comes, the task returns. According to the video, in less than 200 milliseconds and without cold start 05:35.

Failure recovery

The mascot is the axolot, the salamander that regenerates limbs. It represents the idea of regenerating failed agents from a kernel snapshot 05:57.

Example: an agent works 3 hours cleaning data and finds an error. In the classic infrastructure, the three hours are lost. With AX, the agent returns from the last checkpoint. 06:17.

Safety with gViewer

Common containers share the kernel of the machine. A malicious code generated by an agent could in theory compromise the entire machine. 06:59.

gVisor intercepts each agent system call and emulates the kernel in an isolated space, so the code never touches the hardware 07:21.

For production, the video recommends three steps 07:41:

  • isolate with gVisor 08:02;
  • restrict the network with Gateway lists 08:02;
  • pass all traffic through a proxy controlled by people because AX does not alone limit spending on external APIs 08:02.

Other resources

You can describe the simple English environment as "configure a Python 3" development environment. AX delivers the order to an internal agent, Antigravity, who installs the tools before the task begins 08:24.

AX is open source, Apache 2.0 license, and works with kubectl 09:06.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Google AX replace Kubernetes?

Nope. It is a layer of orchestration that runs over the Kubernetes 02:08.

The agent spends processing while waiting for the model?

Nope. The AX suspends the agent by snapshot, and consumption drops to zero until the response arrives. 05:15.

About the video

AI autonomous agents do not behave as traditional microservices or as batch tasks: they accumulate state, perform dynamic loops and require rigorous isolation of security and financial control. In this explanatory video, we analyzed **Google AX**, the open-source declarative orchestration runtime developed by Google to manage and scale workloads of bulk agents.

Understand how AX architecture uses declarative YAML manifestations in the Kubernetes style to simplify infrastructure and solve challenges of resilience, density and failure recovery.
